name: research-report
summary: A short, sourced research report: one agent gathers sources, one writes, one checks every claim against its source before it reaches you.
example: A two-page brief on what EU AI Act obligations apply to a small SaaS company using LLM APIs, with sources
rules: Every claim in the report cites a source in sources.md; a claim without one is cut.
Prefer primary sources (laws, filings, papers, official docs). Quote exactly; never invent a quote, a figure or a source.
Ask the owner only if the goal can be read two ways that lead to different reports.

roles.name: research
roles.does: gathers primary sources with exact quotes
roles.instructions: Find 5-10 sources that answer the goal, primary ones first. For each, add to sources.md: a number, title, link, date checked, and the exact sentences that matter. Hand sources.md to writer with hub_send; find more when writer or checker asks.

roles.name: writer
roles.does: writes the report from the sources, citing each claim
roles.instructions: Wait for research's sources (hub_wait). Write report.md: the answer first, then the reasons, at most two pages, every claim cited as [n] from sources.md. Ask research for what is missing. Hand report.md to checker with hub_send and fix what checker finds.

roles.name: checker
roles.does: checks every claim against its source before the owner sees it
roles.instructions: Wait for writer's report (hub_wait). For every [n], open the source and check that it says what the report claims. Send writer each claim that is wrong, overstated or unsourced. When every claim holds, post with hub_say, addressed to the owner by name (@name): the report is ready, with how many claims you checked and anything still uncertain.
